extracted.intended_audience: literary scholars, narratologists, and graduate students in literary theory
extracted.subtask_description: Analytic framework for studying literary narrative discourse: distinguishing story, narrating, and narrative, and analyzing narrative along the dimensions of tense (order, duration, frequency), mood (modes/degree of representation), and voice (narrating instance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: story, narrative, narrating
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a threefold distinction among the 'story' (histoire), the act of 'narrating' (narration/narrating), and the 'narrative' or narrative discourse (the text itself).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the narrative (the narrated discourse) as the only level directly available to textual analysis in literary narrative; recognize that events and the act of narrating are known only indirectly through traces in the narrative (e.g., first-person pronoun, tense). Avoid conflating the author's life with fictional events or the act of writing with the narrating instance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of narrative discourse analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis should study the relationships between narrative and story, narrative and narrating, and, where inscribed, between story and narrating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the narrative text to reconstruct both events recounted and the narrating act; focus on relationships (not entities) and analyze how narrative mediates knowledge of story and narrating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three analytic classes: tense, mood, voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize analysis into three basic classes: (1) tense — temporal relations between story and narrative; (2) mood — modalities/forms/degrees of representation (mimesis); (3) voice — the narrative situation or narrating instance, including narrator and audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt these classes to determine chapter/section organization; do not hypostatize them (they are relational tools). Note that 'tense' will be treated via Order, Duration, Frequency; 'mood' gathers modalities of representation; 'voice' covers narrating instance and its relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tense: order, duration, frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze temporal relations between story-time and narrative-time along three determinations: order (sequence of events), duration (relative length/speed of telling), and frequency (repetitions in story vs narrative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat each subproblem separately: order concerns permutations and inversions of chronological sequence; duration concerns how much narrative text is devoted to an event; frequency concerns how events' repetition in story maps to repetition in narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mood / modalities of representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate the ways in which the story is perceived and represented by the narrator — the forms and degrees of mimesis ('showing' vs 'telling'), representation of character speech, and explicit/implicit presence of narrator and reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category covers point of view issues traditionally called 'aspect' and parts of 'mood' (in Todorov's terms). Distinguish modes like representation/representation degree, and relate subjective/objective stances to mood analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice (narrative situation / narrating instance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine how the narrating itself is implicated in the narrative: the narrating instance (narrator), its relation to character(s), and the narratorial audience (real or implied).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'voice' broadly (broader than grammatical 'person') to encompass first-/third-person relations and other facets of narrating; base this on Benveniste's 'instance of discourse' and be attentive to the narrating situation as a set of conditions producing the narrative statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order (temporal sequence analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the order in which events or temporal segments are arranged in the narrative discourse with their chronological order in the story (erzählte Zeit vs Erzählzeit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pinpoint and measure discordances; recognize that classical narratives often use in medias res and retrojections. Reconstruct story-order where possible from explicit indicators or inferable clues in the text; do not eliminate either member of the relationship (narrative order or story order) when analyzing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anachrony (discordance between story and narrative orders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any form of temporal discordance between the story's chronological order and the narrative's arrangement of events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'anachrony' as the general term encompassing analepses and prolepses and other discordances; acknowledge that anachrony is a traditional and frequent resource (not a rarity or only modern).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analepsis (retrospection / flashback)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative maneuver that evokes after the fact an event that took place earlier in the story than the current narrative location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label retrospective moves 'analepses'; distinguish subjective vs objective analepses (the latter pertains to narrative-level adoption rather than a character's mental act) — detailed treatment intersects with mood analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prolepsis (anticipation / flashforward)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative maneuver that narrates or evokes in advance an event that will take place later in the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label anticipatory moves 'prolepses'; distinguish subjective vs objective prolepses analogously to analepses; note prolepses' syntactic positions (often at openings of bracketed structures in formulas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjective vs objective anachronies
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate whether an analepsis or prolepsis is adopted by a character's consciousness (subjective) or by the narrative/narrator itself (objective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction is not purely temporal but arises from mood/point-of-view categories; neutral descriptive terms (analepsis/prolepsis) are preferred when avoiding psychological connotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectioning and temporal-position notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide the narrative into distinct sections and assign each a temporal position (e.g., A, B, C with numeric story-positions like 1,2,...), using formulaic notation (e.g., A2-B1-C2) to map narrative order to story order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brackets/parentheses/hyphens to indicate hierarchical subordination, prolepses/analepses, and pure succession (ellipsis). This formal notation helps visualize zigzags, interlockings, and hierarchical dependencies among sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntactic relations between narrative sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze coordination and subordination relations among narrative sections to determine the status (autonomous, subordinate, anticipatory, retrospective) of each section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which sections are autonomous starts, which are subordinate retrospections or anticipations, and how returns to base positions are signaled. Use syntactic markers in the text (e.g., 'he remembered', temporal indicators) to infer these relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipsis (temporal leap without return)
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative acceleration consisting of a leap forward in story-time without any return to the omitted interval; unlike anachrony, it is not a temporal inversion but a mere omission/succession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark transitions that are pure succession with hyphens in notation (C5 - D6); treat ellipses as belonging to duration/speed problems rather than order-problems that produce anachronies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative temporality and pseudo-time (Erzählzeit vs erzählte Zeit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the dual temporality: the time of the story (erzählte Zeit) and the time of the narrative (Erzählzeit), with the narrative's time often functioning as a pseudo-time that stands in for reading/consuming time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for media-specific differences (film and oral narrative permit different kinds of temporal manipulations than written narrative); remember written narrative exists spatially (as text) and its temporality is metonymically borrowed from reading time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological caution: do not hypostatize categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid converting analytical terms (tense, mood, voice) into substantive entities; treat them as relationships and instruments of analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the terms as functional/metaphorical tools (e.g., grammatical metaphors) rather than reifying them; be explicit about the limits of homologies invoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar-metaphor: treat narrative as expansion of a verb
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a grammatical metaphor that treats narrative as a verbal development (amplification of a verb-statement), permitting organization of problems according to categories borrowed from verb grammar (tense, mood, voice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ this metaphor heuristically to formulate the three major analytic classes; do not press presumed homologies too literally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale of analysis: microstructure (micronarrative) vs macrostructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish levels of analysis: micronarrative (fine-grained section-by-section temporal relations) versus macrostructure (large-scale articulations of temporal structure across the work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use crude simplifications when moving to macro-level analysis; details belonging to other scales should be omitted at higher-level descriptions. Examples: detailed A2-B1-C2 zigzag at micro-level vs assigning large narrative blocks to story positions at macro-level.
